html:
The Battle of Siffin was fought in July 657 on the upper Euphrates, in what is now Syria, between the armies of the caliph Ali and of Muawiya, governor of Syria.

Muawiya had refused to accept Ali until the killers of Uthman were punished. Ali led his army from Kufa and camped in front of Muawiya's. Weeks of skirmishes and talks led to a few days of heavy fighting. Ali's side was gaining when, in the best known account, Muawiya's men raised pages of the Quran on their spears and called for the book to decide.

Ali's army made him accept. Two arbitrators were named, and in 658 they met without resolving it. Many of Ali's followers felt he should never have agreed to have men judge God's cause, and they left him as the Kharijites. Ali's authority fell while Muawiya's grew, and in 661 Muawiya took the caliphate. See the First Fitna.
